item.title: Training the People Behind the Claims Assessments: Allstate Claims University
item.description: Late last week, Allstate unveiled Allstate Claims University, a 33,000 square foot campus in Dallas, complete with hands-on property and auto labs—immersive training environments representing scenarios that claims professionals will face in the real world. In a statement about the opening of the campus, Mike Fiato, executive vice president and chief claims officer at Allstate, said, “The investment in Allstate Claims University starts with our people and ends with our customers.” “When someone’s home is damaged by a storm or their vehicle is involved in an accident, they need more than a claim processed: they need an expert who can understand what happened, explain what comes next and help them move forward.” “By investing in our teams, we’re helping ensure customers receive the expertise, care and confidence they need when it matters most,” Fiato said. “The investment in Allstate Claims University starts with our people and ends with our customers.” Allstate reported that the company has 23,000 claims professionals supporting roughly 8.5 million claims each year.

item.title: ERGO becomes official insurance partner of Atlético de Madrid
item.description: ERGO has entered into a multi-year partnership with Atlético de Madrid as the club’s official insurance partner, supporting the insurer’s rebranding of DKV Seguros to ERGO | DKV in Spain. The ERGO | DKV brand will appear on the match and training shorts of Atlético’s men’s and women’s first teams, as well as across stadium advertising, press conferences and the club’s digital channels. ERGO | DKV will also sponsor areas within Atlético’s future Sports City, including its surf academy, and operate a retail location at the development.

item.title: Inszone acquires Hocker Family Insurance
item.description: Inszone Insurance has acquired Hocker Family Insurance, a Morgantown, Kentucky-based insurance agency founded in 1926. The fourth-generation agency offers personal, commercial, life, and health insurance. The deal expands Inszone’s presence in Kentucky and follows several recent acquisitions by the Sacramento-based brokerage, including Two Fong’s in California and Radwick & Lightle in Washington.

item.title: Sompo launches new global website
item.description: Sompo has launched sompo.com, a new corporate website that brings its businesses across North America, the UK and Continental Europe under a unified digital presence. “Our new website is an important expression of the Sompo brand and how we want to be understood by our audiences. As our global business continues to evolve, the website will play a key role in helping us present a consistent narrative around our purpose, our expertise and the distinctive value we bring to our customers, partners and talent.” – Group Head of Communications, Sina Martens.

item.title: FactorLab Turns Workplace Language into Risk Signals
item.description: FactorLab sees a possible analogue in commercial workplace risk. (Image credit: IIR/Gemini.) Commercial insurers have long relied on inspections, documentation and loss history to understand how effectively an insured manages workplace risk. FactorLab (Pleasanton, Calif.) believes another potentially valuable source of risk information has largely gone untapped: what workers and supervisors actually say while preparing to do the work.

item.title: Blenheim launches Knot-on-Time
item.description: Blenheim Partnerships, part of White Bear Group, has launched Knot-on-Time, an insurance solution protecting vessel owners against losses caused by the delayed delivery or non-delivery of newly built ships. The product was developed and is led by Edward Parker, senior underwriter for special risks at Blenheim Partnerships. The coverage can address higher vessel-replacement costs, lost charter income, financing expenses, contractual liabilities and mitigation costs associated with securing alternative tonnage or commissioning a replacement vessel.

item.title: SafetyCulture rebrands as Mitti
item.description: Australian workplace operations platform SafetyCulture has rebranded as Mitti , marking what the Australian company calls the biggest transformation in its history. In 2020, SafetyCulture and QBE launched Mitti Insurance , a joint venture combining small business insurance with virtual risk assessments and workplace-safety tools. Now, SafetyCulture has become Mitti, while SafetyCulture Care has returned to the Mitti Insurance name.

item.title: Hawaii Faces Rare Hurricane Strike as Storms Batter Indiana
item.description: Hawaii is in line for a rare hurricane strike as Tropical Storm Lala grazes the Big Island, while severe storms threaten more flooding and outages across Indiana. This would be the first hurricane strike anywhere in Hawaii since Iniki in 1992. Related: Hawaii Faces More Tropical Threats From El Niño-Charged Pacific In the Midwest, nearly 200,000 homes and businesses are without power across Indiana after days of severe weather disrupted air travel and caused widespread flooding and damage.

item.title: Hackers Claim Mass Data Theft From Shell, Philips, GE, Fiserv And Dozens of Others
item.description: A prolific hacking group known for exploiting software vulnerabilities to attack multiple targets simultaneously claimed it had stolen large volumes of data from nearly 50 companies worldwide, including Philips, Shell, Fiserv and GE, according to a posting on the group’s website. Philips said it had been targeted by Cl0p while Shell said it was aware of a recent “possible incident,” confirming an earlier report on Thursday by Dutch media outlet BNR. “Philips has identified and contained an attempted cybersecurity compromise of a specific enterprise server related to internal data,” Philips said in a statement, adding that the incident does not impact customer environments.

item.title: Driving Above the Speed Limit Costs You, Doesn’t Save Much Time
item.description: More than 43% of the studied trips included at least one instance of speeding, and drivers spent nearly 12% of their driving time going faster than the speed limit. They found that if drivers of light-duty, conventional internal combustion engine vehicles actually drove at posted speed limits, it could save an average of $22 million, based on fuel costs at the time, 6.7 million gallons of fuel, and 57,000 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide every day. If your objective is to get to your destination safely and to save fuel, then you might drive slower than the speed limit,” said William Northrop, mechanical engineering professor at the University of Minnesota and study co-author.

item.title: Gen Z Drivers Most Likely to Drive Uninsured: TransUnion
item.description: Nearly one-third of Gen Z drivers (30%) admitted having owned or driven an uninsured vehicle over the past six months, making them the most likely generation to own or drive a vehicle without coverage, according to new research from TransUnion. The TransUnion’s Q3 2026 Insurance Personal Lines Trends and Perspectives Quarterly Snapshot explores the challenge of identifying Gen Z drivers at risk of coverage lapse. Telematics may also be a stronger incentive to help younger safe drivers feel more in control of their rates and more likely to maintain coverage, the report added.

item.title: Insurance Regulators Get Schooled on AI Governance
item.description: Insurance regulators are moving artificial intelligence governance from the policy manual into the examination file. 13) at its Summer National Meeting , the National Association of Insurance Commissioners provided an update on its AI Risk Evaluation Supplement , a structured set of inquiries designed to help state regulators examine how insurers use and oversee AI. The supplement isn’t a certification program, a rating system or a new insurance law.

item.title: Bermuda Stock Exchange market share grows, with now $70.5bn cat bond and ILS listings
item.description: The Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) continued to grow its market share of catastrophe bonds and other insurance-linked securities (ILS) in the second-quarter of 2026, ending the period with a record-high $70.5 billion of ILS related listings on the exchange. It represents continued growth in the total dollar value of insurance-linked securities related listings on the Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX). While the BSX also expanded its market share slightly in the second quarter as well, cementing its key role as a venue for listing catastrophe bond and ILS securities.

item.title: Lala takes aim at Hawaii, could become first US hurricane landfall of 2026
item.description: Tropical storm Lala in the central Pacific could make the first United States hurricane landfall of 2026 this weekend, as the storm is forecast to intensify and has the Big Island of Hawaii in its sights. Which would make Lala the first US hurricane landfall of 2026, should that occur. You can see tropical storm Lala’s latest position and the forecast wind speed intensities below, thanks to Tomer Burg’s excellent PolarWX resources: Lala could either give the Big Island of Hawaii a glancing blow or make a direct landfall it seems, perhaps also affecting other islands in the chain.

item.title: Talanx raises 2026 profit outlook after strong first-half net income of €1.5bn
item.description: Talanx Group, a major German financial services and insurance company, has announced its financial results for the first half of 2026, reporting a record-breaking net income of EUR 1.499 billion. The first half of 2026 experienced a number of losses from natural disasters, with the largest being Winter Storm “Fern” in the USA and Canada (EUR 132 million) and the Atlantic storms on the Iberian Peninsula and in Morocco (EUR 127 million). Profit growth was observed in all divisions, with Primary Insurance contributing 52% to Group net income.

item.title: Milliman appoints Jim Fulton as next CEO
item.description: Milliman, Inc., a global actuarial and consulting firm, has announced that Jim Fulton will become its next Chief Executive Officer (CEO). Fulton has served as Milliman’s Chief Financial Officer since 2015, where he has played a role in the firm’s organic growth and mergers and acquisitions strategy. I’m looking forward to helping shape Milliman’s future as we continue to grow and evolve,” said Fulton Fulton’s appointment comes as the firm continues to develop from its actuarial origins into a broader consultancy providing risk management and technology solutions.

item.title: Aviva H1’26 operating profit exceeds £1.3bn as GI premiums increase 29%
item.description: British insurer Aviva has announced its financial results for the first half of 2026, reporting Group operating profit of £1.326 billion, up 24% from £1.068 billion in H1 2025. Amanda Blanc, Group Chief Executive Officer, commented: “Aviva’s results in the first half of 2026 were very strong, with operating profit up 24% to £1.3 billion. Meanwhile, Aviva’s Canada division posted a 3% rise in general insurance premiums to £2.183 billion, compared to H1 2025’s £2.149 billion, and undiscounted COR of 93.0%, compared to the 94.7% in H1 2025.

item.title: Trump ‘Energy Emergency’ Could Fast-Track Expansion of Louisiana LNG Export Terminal
item.description: Less than two years after opening, a liquefied natural gas terminal near New Orleans is seeking a multi-billion-dollar expansion under a new Trump administration “emergency” permitting process that shortens environmental review and may weaken protections for surrounding wetlands and waterways. Army Corps of Engineers granted Plaquemines LNG, on the Mississippi River between Myrtle Grove and Port Sulphur, fast-tracked permitting under a ” national energy emergency ” President Donald Trump declared last year. Hundreds of other energy projects could receive expedited permitting under the emergency declaration, which Trump said was necessary to maintain a “reliable, diversified, and affordable supply of energy” for the U.S.

item.title: Kansas Town Settles Lawsuit with Former Reporter Over Controversial Police Raid
item.description: A small Kansas town has agreed to pay $850,000 to a former reporter at its weekly newspaper to end her federal lawsuit over a police raid of the paper’s offices in 2023 that ignited a national furor over press freedom. Now-retired Marion County Record reporter Phyllis Zorn said in her lawsuit that the raid violated press freedoms and protections from unreasonable law enforcement searches guaranteed by the U.S. Zorn’s attorney, Randy Rathbun, and an attorney for the city Marion, Jennifer Hill, filed a joint statement Tuesday — the third anniversary of the raid on the newspaper’s offices — that Zorn’s lawsuit was being dismissed.

item.title: Tyson to Close More Beef Plants as Cattle Shortage Drags On
item.description: is closing more beef plants as a prolonged cattle shortage continues to force the US beefpacking industry’s restructuring. Production at the affected facilities will be absorbed by other plants, and Tyson now plans to anchor its beef operation around just three plants: in Nebraska, Kansas and Texas. The Illinois and Washington beef plants process about 5,000 heads of cattle per day, according to a note from Barclays analysts led by Benjamin Theurer.

item.title: AIG, Parametrix launch parametric cover for cloud outage losses
item.description: New cyber solution provides faster payouts for business interruption caused by cloud service disruptions AIG and Parametrix have launched a parametric cloud outage solution designed to help businesses recover losses from cloud service outages and technology provider downtime. Rather than relying on a traditional claims assessment, the coverage uses a predefined parametric formula to evaluate cloud service downtime and its potential financial impact. AIG said the coverage also allows cyber and cloud outage protection to be managed under a single policy.

item.title: Faye raises $50 million to expand AI-powered travel insurance platform
item.description: Series C brings Faye’s total funding to $100 million as the company targets greater automation across underwriting, assistance and claims Travel insurance technology company Faye has raised $50 million in Series C funding , bringing its total capital raised to $100 million as it expands its AI-powered travel protection platform. Founded in 2022, Faye combines travel insurance, financial services, real-time travel intelligence and traveler assistance through a single platform. The funding will support Faye’s international expansion, partnerships with online travel agencies, airlines, cruise companies and other travel brands, as well as further development of its AI capabilities.

item.title: Ambrook raises $30 million
item.description: Financial management platform Ambrook has raised a $30 million Series B led by former Stripe executive Lachy Groom, bringing its total funding to $59 million. Founded in 2020, Ambrook provides accounting, payments and cash-management tools to independent businesses in agriculture, trucking, construction and property management. Ambrook now serves more than 8,000 businesses across all 50 states, up from around 2,500 in July 2025.

item.title: Allstate opens claims training campus in Dallas
item.description: Allstate has opened Allstate Claims University, a 33,000-square-foot training campus in Dallas designed for the insurer’s 23,000 claims professionals, who handle approximately 8.5 million claims annually. According to Allstate, the hands-on training is intended to improve damage assessments and prepare claims teams for increasingly complex homes, vehicles and repair technologies. “The investment in Allstate Claims University starts with our people and ends with our customers.

item.title: Amynta Group to acquire Southern States’ insurance operations
item.description: Amynta Group , an insurance services company that operates MGAs and specialty underwriting businesses, has agreed to acquire Southern States Underwriters and SSC Insurance Agency, the insurance operations of Southern States Cooperative. Founded in 1953, Southern States Underwriters is a managing general underwriter specializing in commercial property and casualty insurance for suppliers, distributors, and service providers in the agricultural industry. It also serves as attorney-in-fact and exclusive distribution partner for Southern States Insurance Exchange, a reciprocal focused on agribusiness risks.

item.title: Show Your Adjusters They Matter to Combat Claims Burnout
item.description: View Series There’s an inconvenient trend that insurers are facing today: claims adjusters are burning out, leaving their jobs at concerning rates. But when workflows prioritize speed over field support, adjusters race through complex claims — producing documentation gaps and file revisions. Field-native technology that turns real-time observation directly into structured, priced documentation shrinks that gap to zero — letting adjusters close a file before they leave the driveway instead of after dinner.

item.title: Thoma Bravo to Take Accelerant Private in $4 Billion Deal
item.description: Accelerant said on Thursday that private equity firm Thoma Bravo will take the insurance marketplace platform private in an all-cash deal worth more than $4 billion, just over a year after its New York listing. “We cut the noise, crush inefficiencies, and fuel profitable growth – for MGAs, capital partners, and the businesses they serve.” “Accelerant has built something rare in specialty insurance,” said Matt LoSardo, a principal at Thoma Bravo. Thoma Bravo, a software-focused investment firm managing more than $172 billion in assets as of March 31, has invested in insurance technology and data businesses for years.

item.title: Samoa adaptation plan calls for regional cat bond, expansion of Pacific parametric coverage
item.description: A national adaptation plan produced for the government of south Pacific island nation Samoa calls for scaling up of parametric protection across the region, as well as for existing risk pools to cover more perils, while also suggesting a regional catastrophe bond should be planned to provide risk capacity in future. On the potential for a regional Pacific catastrophe bond, Samoa’s new adaptation plan calls for “exploration of a regional catastrophe bond tranche by 2040.” Presumably this could be either a multi-country catastrophe bond, issued by a development bank for example, or a cat bond to support the reinsurance needs of PCRIC or a risk pool established under PCRAFI 2.0. This could involve an increase in parametric insurance limits being made available, while the plan also calls for expansion of the PCRAFI initiatives coverage to include additional perils.

item.title: AIG launches parametric cloud outage insurance working with Parametrix
item.description: Global insurer AIG has expanded its cyber offering with the launch of a new parametric cloud outage solution developed in partnership with Parametrix, a provider of digital infrastructure insurance solutions. As mentioned, AIG’s new parametric cloud outage solution was developed in partnership with Parametrix, with the parametric formula backed by Parametrix’s proprietary monitoring of more than 750 data centers globally and tracking over 9,000 software and other technology providers. Moreover, AIG’s new Parametric Cloud Outage Solution triggers are based on a predefined formula that considers cloud service downtime and the associated potential financial impact.

item.title: US severe convective storm (SCS) industry losses exceed $35bn in 2026 so far: Gallagher Re
item.description: According to reinsurance broker Gallagher Re, year-to-date industry losses from US severe convective storms in 2026 have accelerated and climbed above $35 billion, as the peril’s quieter start to the opening months of the year have since given way to prolific activity. This marks a sharp increase from mid-June where Gallagher Re had estimated that insurance industry losses from severe convective storms in the United States this year had already topped $22 billion. In addition, Gallagher Re’s report states that at least six SCS outbreaks in 2026 have resulted in a multi-billion-dollar industry loss; only behind 2023 (11), 2024 (10), and 2025 (7).

item.title: RiverStone International and QBE agree $1.6bn LTP reinsurance agreements
item.description: Legacy reinsurance and run-off specialist RiverStone International has entered into loss portfolio transfer (LPT) agreements with QBE Insurance Group, r epresenting approximately US$1.6 billion in reserves, further strengthening the long-standing partnership between both companies. Paul Brockman, Group Chief Executive Officer of RiverStone International, said: “ We are pleased to have entered into these transactions with QBE Insurance Group, further strengthening a long-standing relationship built on delivering tailored legacy solutions across multiple lines of business and jurisdictions. “These transactions demonstrate the breadth of RiverStone International’s capabilities and the strength of our global platform in providing finality and certainty for complex long-tail liabilities.

item.title: Korean Re Q2’26 net income rises 77.6% amid stronger underwriting and investment results
item.description: Korean Re, South Korea’s specialist reinsurance company, reported higher profit for the first half of 2026, supported by improved reinsurance performance and stronger investment results. Net income increased 77.6% to KRW 347.3 billion from KRW 195.5 billion, reflecting improvements in both insurance and investment profit. The reinsurer’s revenue from insurance and investment increased 4.2% year on year to KRW 3,652.1 billion in the three months to June 2026, compared with KRW 3,503.5 billion in the same period of 2025.

item.title: Crypto Firm Trezor Says Data Breach Exposed Thousands of Clients
item.description: Trezor, a maker of hardware devices used to store cryptocurrencies, said personal information belonging to thousands of customers was exposed in a data breach affecting one of its shipping providers, the latest security incident to hit the digital-asset industry. Unfortunately, one of our shipping providers has experienced a data breach that exposed sensitive order data. The Trezor incident comes on the heels of a breach involving another hardware-wallet maker, Toronto-based Coinkite Inc., adding concerns about the heightened risks crypto holders face, even when taking all the recommended precautions to secure their assets.
